Element / Feature: Sign in and land on the console
Test Steps: 1. Sign in with an admin account. 2. Open /ops. 3. Note where it lands.
Test Data: Admin account
Expected Result: The console opens on the dashboard. The customer app chrome, such as the bottom bar and support button, is not present.

Element / Feature: Customer account cannot open the console
Test Steps: 1. Sign in as a customer. 2. Type the console address in the browser.
Test Data: Customer account
Expected Result: The customer is returned to the customer app. No ops data is shown even briefly.

Element / Feature: Agent account cannot open the console
Test Steps: 1. Sign in as an agent. 2. Type the console address in the browser.
Test Data: Agent account
Expected Result: The agent is returned to the agent app.

Element / Feature: Signed-out visitor cannot open the console
Test Steps: 1. Sign out. 2. Open the console address directly. 3. Also try a deep link to a specific order.
Test Data: No session; then a direct order URL
Expected Result: Both lead to sign-in. Nothing about any order is visible before signing in.

Test Steps: 1. Open the dashboard. 2. Note each count. 3. Open the matching board and count the rows.
Test Data: Orders spread across pickups, drop-offs and dispatched
Expected Result: Every count on the dashboard matches the board it points to.

Test Steps: 1. Open the dashboard on an environment with no orders.
Test Data: No orders in the system
Expected Result: Zeroes and empty states are shown with an explanation. No spinner that never resolves and no error.

Test Steps: 1. Have a customer complete a signup. 2. Open the dashboard. 3. Open the verifications section and then one account's documents.
Test Data: One account with documents pending review
Expected Result: The account appears in the pending list and its documents open for review.

Test Steps: 1. Approve one account's documents. 2. Reject another with a reason. 3. Check each customer's own screen.
Test Data: Two accounts pending review
Expected Result: The approved customer can book. The rejected one is told which document was refused and can replace it.

Test Steps: 1. Have a customer request a cancellation. 2. Open the dashboard. 3. Approve it. 4. Have another request one and reject it.
Test Data: Two orders with cancellation requests
Expected Result: The approved order becomes cancelled and the rejected one keeps its stage. Each customer sees the outcome on their own order.

Element / Feature: Each board shows its own work
Test Steps: 1. Open each board in turn. 2. Pick one order and check whether it appears on any other board.
Test Data: Orders in the pickup, drop-off and dispatched lanes
Expected Result: Each board shows only its own lane and no order appears on two boards at once.

Test Steps: 1. Read one card in full. 2. Compare it with the same order's detail page.
Test Data: Any order on the board
Expected Result: The card shows the order number, customer, route, dates, payment method and agent, and every value matches the detail page.

Element / Feature: Cards and table views on desktop
Test Steps: 1. At a desktop width switch from cards to the table. 2. Compare what each shows. 3. Switch back.
Test Data: Viewport 1440 x 900
Expected Result: Both views list the same orders and the table adds a stage column. Switching does not lose the current filters.

Test Steps: 1. Open the board on a phone. 2. Scroll a long list. 3. Open the More menu.
Test Data: Viewport 390 x 844
Expected Result: The board is usable one-handed, nothing overflows sideways, and Transactions and Users are both reachable from More.

Test Steps: 1. Filter down to something with no matches.
Test Data: A filter combination matching nothing
Expected Result: An empty state explains there is nothing to show and offers to clear the filters. Not a blank area.

Test Steps: 1. Keep the pickups board open. 2. Have a customer book a pickup. 3. Watch the board.
Test Data: A new booking made while the board is open
Expected Result: The new order appears on the board without the page having to be reloaded by hand.

Test Steps: 1. Have someone book as a guest. 2. Open the pickups board and find that order.
Test Data: One guest booking, one account booking
Expected Result: Both appear. The guest order shows the guest's name and phone, not an empty customer column.

Element / Feature: Filters stay out of the way by default
Test Steps: 1. Open a board fresh. 2. Note whether any filter panel is open. 3. Open the filter control on desktop, then on a phone.
Test Data: Fresh session; desktop then phone
Expected Result: No filter panel is open to begin with. The control opens a panel on desktop and a sheet on a phone.

Test Steps: 1. Filter by each stage in turn. 2. Return to All.
Test Data: Stages: inbound, at hub, settled, all
Expected Result: Only orders at the chosen stage remain, and All brings back the full list.

Test Steps: 1. Filter to assigned. 2. Filter to unassigned.
Test Data: A board holding both assigned and unassigned pickups
Expected Result: Assigned lists only orders that already have an agent, and unassigned only those without one.

Test Steps: 1. Filter booking date by today, then the last 7 days, then the last 30 days. 2. Spot-check the dates on the cards.
Test Data: Booking date: today, 7 days, 30 days
Expected Result: Only orders booked in the chosen window are listed, and the ranges offered look backwards in time.

Test Steps: 1. Switch the date field to pickup date. 2. Filter by today, tomorrow and this week.
Test Data: Pickup date: today, tomorrow, this week
Expected Result: The ranges offered now look forwards in time, and switching the field does not leave a range selected that makes no sense for it.

Test Steps: 1. Filter by each payment method in turn.
Test Data: Pay now, pay at pickup, pay at drop-off, COD
Expected Result: Each filter lists only orders on that method, and COD orders are labelled the same way here as on the order itself.

Element / Feature: Active filters are visible and removable
Test Steps: 1. Apply three filters at once. 2. Read the count on the filter control. 3. Remove one using its chip. 4. Clear all.
Test Data: Stage at hub; unassigned; COD
Expected Result: The count reads three, each applied filter shows as a removable chip, removing one changes only that filter, and Clear all returns to the plain board.

Test Steps: 1. Apply filters. 2. Open an order from the board. 3. Go back to the board.
Test Data: Any two filters applied
Expected Result: The board comes back with the same filters still applied, not reset to the default view.

Test Steps: 1. Search for a full order number. 2. Then search for part of one.
Test Data: A known order number, then the last four characters of it
Expected Result: Both find the order. The list narrows as the tester types rather than needing a separate search button press.

Test Steps: 1. Search a customer name. 2. Search a phone number.
Test Data: A known customer name and their phone number
Expected Result: Both find that customer's orders.

Element / Feature: Search reaches beyond the first page
Test Steps: 1. On a board with well over a thousand orders, search for an order known to be old and far down the list.
Test Data: A board with more than 1000 orders; an order from the very oldest
Expected Result: The old order is found. Search covers the whole board, not only the part already loaded on screen.

Test Steps: 1. Search a term with a known number of matches. 2. Read the caption above the list.
Test Data: A search term matching a known count
Expected Result: The caption states the true number of matches, which may be larger than the number of rows currently on screen.

Test Steps: 1. Search for something that cannot match.
Test Data: Search: zzzzzzzz
Expected Result: An empty state says nothing matched and offers to clear the search. The previous results are not left on screen.

Test Steps: 1. Apply a stage filter. 2. Search within it. 3. Clear the search but keep the filter.
Test Data: Stage at hub, plus a customer name
Expected Result: The search runs inside the filter, and clearing the search leaves the filter in place.

Test Steps: 1. Export the board. 2. Open the file in Google Sheets. 3. Compare the first rows against the screen.
Test Data: Any board with orders
Expected Result: The file downloads and opens with proper column headings, and the first rows match the board.

Test Steps: 1. Open a board with well over a thousand matching orders. 2. Export. 3. Count the rows in the file.
Test Data: A board with more than 1000 matching orders
Expected Result: Every matching order is in the file. It does not stop at a round number such as 1000.

Element / Feature: Export follows the filters and sort
Test Steps: 1. Apply a stage filter and a date filter and set the sort. 2. Export. 3. Compare the file against the board.
Test Data: Stage at hub; last 7 days; sorted oldest first
Expected Result: The file holds exactly the filtered orders in the same order as the board, not the whole unfiltered board.

Test Steps: 1. Set a wide date range. 2. Export. 3. Compare the totals and dates against the screen.
Test Data: A range covering a large number of transactions
Expected Result: Every transaction in range is exported and the amounts and dates match the ledger exactly.

Test Steps: 1. Have a booking made under a name with a comma and a quotation mark. 2. Export the board. 3. Open the file in Google Sheets.
Test Data: Customer name: Sharma, Rajesh "Raju"
Expected Result: The name lands in one column with its punctuation intact. It does not spill into the next column or split the row.

Test Steps: 1. Choose a date range with no transactions. 2. Export.
Test Data: A date range known to hold nothing
Expected Result: Either the export is offered with headings and no rows, or it is clearly refused. No empty or corrupt file is downloaded silently.

Test Steps: 1. Open an order in a late stage. 2. Read every section.
Test Data: An order that has been weighed or settled
Expected Result: Customer, sender, receiver, parcel, payment, agent, stage history and documents are all filled in, with every date shown in India time.

Test Steps: 1. Open an order from a customer who uploaded KYC. 2. Open each document.
Test Data: An order with KYC documents
Expected Result: Each document opens and is readable, and it belongs to the customer on this order.

Element / Feature: Assign a pickup to an agent
Test Steps: 1. Open an unassigned pickup. 2. Choose an agent and assign. 3. Check the agent's own app.
Test Data: An unassigned pickup and an active agent
Expected Result: The order moves on by itself, shows the agent's name, and appears in that agent's job list.

Element / Feature: Agent picker only offers active agents
Test Steps: 1. Open the agent picker on an unassigned pickup. 2. Look for an agent known to be inactive.
Test Data: One active agent and one inactive agent
Expected Result: Only active agents are listed. An inactive one cannot be chosen.

Test Steps: 1. Open the same order on two machines as two admins. 2. Assign a different agent on each at the same moment.
Test Data: One order, two admins, two agents
Expected Result: One assignment takes effect and the other admin is told the order has already moved. The order ends up with exactly one agent.

Test Steps: 1. Assign an order to one agent. 2. Reassign it to another. 3. Check both agents' apps.
Test Data: Two active agents
Expected Result: The order moves to the second agent and disappears from the first agent's list.

Test Steps: 1. Open a drop-off order. 2. Ask the customer for the drop-off code. 3. Enter a wrong code. 4. Enter the correct one.
Test Data: The customer's drop-off code; wrong code 000000
Expected Result: The wrong code is refused with a clear message. The correct code marks the parcel received at the hub.

Test Steps: 1. Open a received order. 2. Enter the weighed weight, heavier than booked. 3. Confirm.
Test Data: Booked 2 kg; weighed 3.5 kg
Expected Result: The new price is worked out and shown, the difference against the booked amount is clear, and the customer can see the change on their own order.

Test Steps: 1. Weigh a parcel lighter than booked. 2. Confirm.
Test Data: Booked 3 kg; weighed 2 kg
Expected Result: The price is recalculated and any amount owed back to the customer is shown rather than being quietly kept.

Test Steps: 1. Open a weighed order with an amount outstanding. 2. Record the collection. 3. Read the order and the ledger.
Test Data: An order with a balance after reweighing
Expected Result: The order shows as settled and the collection appears in the transactions ledger with the right amount.

Test Steps: 1. Open a settled order. 2. Generate the docket. 3. Open it.
Test Data: A settled order
Expected Result: The docket is produced with the right order and customer details and the order moves to ready for dispatch.

Test Steps: 1. Open orders at four different stages. 2. Note which actions are offered on each.
Test Data: One order at each of: awaiting pickup, received, weighed, dispatched
Expected Result: Only the actions that make sense at that stage are offered. Nothing lets an order skip a step or go backwards.

Element / Feature: Acting on an order refreshes the board
Test Steps: 1. Filter the board to unassigned. 2. Assign an agent to one of the orders shown. 3. Return to the board.
Test Data: Board filtered to unassigned
Expected Result: The order has left the unassigned list without the page needing a manual reload.

Test Steps: 1. Open the ledger. 2. Read a row in full. 3. Open the order it belongs to.
Test Data: Several settled orders
Expected Result: Each row shows the amount, the method, who collected it and when, and the order it points to matches.

Test Steps: 1. Set the range to today. 2. Widen it to the last 30 days. 3. Compare the totals.
Test Data: Today, then 30 days
Expected Result: The list and the total both change with the range, and the wider range is never smaller than the narrower one.

Test Steps: 1. Have an agent collect on two jobs. 2. Open the ledger and find both. 3. Compare with the agent's own collections screen.
Test Data: Two collections by one agent, for example 1200 and 800
Expected Result: Both appear against that agent's name and the totals agree with the agent's own screen.

Test Steps: 1. Filter to a small range. 2. Add the row amounts by hand. 3. Compare with the total shown.
Test Data: A range holding fewer than twenty transactions
Expected Result: The total shown equals the sum of the rows.

Test Steps: 1. Open the users screen. 2. Read the roles.
Test Data: Several staff accounts across roles
Expected Result: Every staff account is listed with the right role, and customers are not mixed into this list.

Test Steps: 1. Change a staff member's role. 2. Have that person sign in again.
Test Data: One staff account
Expected Result: The new role takes effect on their next sign-in and they land on the surface that matches it.

Test Steps: 1. Deactivate an agent. 2. Open an unassigned pickup and check the agent picker. 3. Check the jobs that agent already holds.
Test Data: An agent with one job in hand
Expected Result: The deactivated agent no longer appears in the picker, and what happens to their existing job is stated rather than left ambiguous.

Element / Feature: Dates are in India time everywhere
Test Steps: 1. Note the date and time on one order card. 2. Compare it on the table view, the detail page and the exported file.
Test Data: One order with a known booking time
Expected Result: All four show the same India time. None is shifted by five and a half hours.

Test Steps: 1. Note an amount on a card. 2. Compare it on the detail page, the ledger and the export.
Test Data: One order with a known amount
Expected Result: Every place shows the same amount in Indian rupee formatting. No raw or unformatted numbers.

Test Steps: 1. Just after midnight India time, filter booking date by today. 2. Check an order booked late yesterday evening and one booked minutes ago.
Test Data: Tested shortly after midnight IST; one order at 23:30 yesterday, one at 00:10 today
Expected Result: Only the order booked after midnight is included. The day turns over at midnight India time.

Test Steps: 1. Sort newest first and check the top row. 2. Sort oldest first and check it again. 3. Export and check the file order.
Test Data: A board with orders spread over several weeks
Expected Result: The order reverses correctly on screen and the exported file follows the same order.

Element / Feature: Long values do not break the layout
Test Steps: 1. Find or create an order with a very long customer or company name. 2. View it as a card and in the table.
Test Data: A company name over 60 characters
Expected Result: The name is wrapped or shortened neatly. It does not push the layout sideways or hide other columns.

Element / Feature: Console after a long idle period
Test Steps: 1. Leave the console open for an hour. 2. Come back and use it.
Test Data: Console left open and idle
Expected Result: Either the data refreshes or the console asks the user to sign in again. It never shows stale figures as if they were current.
